# nxos_ospfv3 (Resource)

This resource can manage the OSPFv3 configuration on NX-OS devices, including OSPFv3 instances, VRFs, areas, and interface settings.

### API Documentation

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "nxos_ospfv3" "example" {
  admin_state = "enabled"
  instances = {
    "OSPFv3" = {
      admin_state  = "enabled"
      flush_routes = false
      isolate      = false
      vrfs = {
        "VRF1" = {
          admin_state               = "enabled"
          bandwidth_reference       = 400000
          bandwidth_reference_unit  = "mbps"
          router_id                 = "34.56.78.90"
          bfd_control               = false
          log_adjacency_changes     = "brief"
          discard_route_external    = false
          discard_route_internal    = false
          name_lookup               = true
          passive_interface_default = false
          areas = {
            "0.0.0.10" = {
              redistribute             = false
              nssa_translator_role     = "always"
              summary                  = false
              suppress_forward_address = false
              type                     = "regular"
              address_families = {
                "ipv6-ucast" = {
                  cost = "10"
                  ranges = {
                    "2001:db8::/32" = {
                      cost    = "10"
                      control = "no-advertise"
                    }
                  }
                }
              }
            }
          }
          address_families = {
            "ipv6-ucast" = {
              administrative_distance       = "10"
              default_metric                = "1024"
              default_route_nssa_pbit_clear = true
              max_ecmp_cost                 = 16
              redistributions = {
                "direct;none;none" = {
                  route_map        = "RM_REDIST"
                  srv6_prefix_type = "unspecified"
                }
              }
              default_information_originate_always    = true
              default_information_originate_route_map = "RM_DEFAULT"
              spf_throttle_hold_interval              = 100
              spf_throttle_initial_interval           = 10
              spf_throttle_max_interval               = 3000
              summary_addresses = {
                "2001:db8:1::/48" = {
                  tag = 5
                }
              }
            }
          }
          lsa_arrival_interval        = 50
          lsa_group_pacing_interval   = 20
          lsa_throttle_hold_interval  = 50
          lsa_throttle_max_interval   = 3000
          lsa_throttle_start_interval = 10
          graceful_restart_control    = "planned-only"
          graceful_restart_period     = 30
          graceful_restart_helper     = false
        }
      }
    }
  }
  interfaces = {
    "eth1/4" = {
      advertise_secondaries = false
      area                  = "0.0.0.10"
      bfd_control           = "disabled"
      cost                  = 1000
      dead_interval         = 60
      hello_interval        = 15
      network_type          = "p2p"
      passive               = "enabled"
      priority              = 10
      admin_state           = "enabled"
      instance_name         = "OSPFv3"
      instance_id           = 1
      mtu_ignore            = true
      retransmit_interval   = 10
      transmit_delay        = 5
    }
  }
}
```

## Schema

### Optional

- `admin_state` (String) The administrative state of the object or policy.
  - Choices: `enabled`, `disabled`
- `deletion_policy` (String) What happens on the device when objects managed by the resource are removed. `delete` deletes the object on destroy, including any configuration not managed by Terraform, and deletes single child objects once none of their attributes are configured anymore, unless the device holds other entries below them. `reset` deletes the objects created by the resource on destroy, resets the managed attributes of the objects that already existed and leaves configuration not managed by Terraform in place. `retain` leaves the device unchanged on destroy and only removes the resource from the state. Overrides the `deletion_policy` of the provider, which defaults to `delete`. See the [Deletion Policy](../guides/deletion_policy) guide for details.
  - Choices: `delete`, `reset`, `retain`
- `device` (String) A device name from the provider configuration.
- `instances` (Attributes Map) List of OSPFv3 instances.
  - Map key: `name` - OSPFv3 instance name. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--instances))
- `interfaces` (Attributes Map) List of OSPFv3 interface configurations.
  - Map key: `interface_id` - Must match first field in the output of `show intf brief`. Example: `eth1/1`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--interfaces))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The distinguished name of the object.

<a id="nestedatt--instances"></a>
### Nested Schema for `instances`

Optional:

- `admin_state` (String) The administrative state of the object or policy.
  - Choices: `enabled`, `disabled`
- `flush_routes` (Boolean) Flush routes on non-graceful controlled restart.
- `isolate` (Boolean) Isolate this router from OSPFv3 perspective.
- `vrfs` (Attributes Map) List of OSPFv3 VRFs.
  - Map key: `name` - VRF name. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--instances--vrfs))

<a id="nestedatt--instances--vrfs"></a>
### Nested Schema for `instances.vrfs`

Optional:

- `address_families` (Attributes Map) List of OSPFv3 address families.
  - Map key: `address_family_type` - IPv6 unicast address family type.
  - Key choices: `ipv6-ucast` (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--instances--vrfs--address_families))
- `admin_state` (String) OSPFv3 VRF administrative state.
  - Choices: `enabled`, `disabled`
- `areas` (Attributes Map) List of OSPFv3 areas.
  - Map key: `area_id` - Area Id as an integer or ip address. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--instances--vrfs--areas))
- `bandwidth_reference` (Number) Bandwidth reference value, holds the range from 1-4000000 if unit is mbps and holds range from 1-4000 if unit is gbps.
  - Range: `0`-`4294967295`
- `bandwidth_reference_unit` (String) Bandwidth reference unit (Mbps or Gbps).
  - Choices: `mbps`, `gbps`
- `bfd_control` (Boolean) Holds the controls for bfd.
- `discard_route_external` (Boolean) Holds the controls for discard-route external.
- `discard_route_internal` (Boolean) Holds the controls for discard-route internal.
- `graceful_restart_control` (String) Graceful restart controls like planned, complete and disabled state.
  - Choices: `planned-only`, `complete`, `disabled`
- `graceful_restart_helper` (Boolean) Graceful restart helper mode.
- `graceful_restart_period` (Number) Graceful restart period in seconds starting from 5 to 1800.
  - Range: `5`-`1800`
- `log_adjacency_changes` (String) Adjacency change logging level.
  - Choices: `none`, `brief`, `detail`
- `lsa_arrival_interval` (Number) Minimum interval between arrival of a LSA.
  - Range: `10`-`600000`
- `lsa_group_pacing_interval` (Number) LSA group pacing interval.
  - Range: `1`-`1800`
- `lsa_throttle_hold_interval` (Number) LSA generation throttle hold interval.
  - Range: `50`-`30000`
- `lsa_throttle_max_interval` (Number) LSA generation throttle maximum interval.
  - Range: `50`-`30000`
- `lsa_throttle_start_interval` (Number) LSA generation throttle start wait interval.
  - Range: `0`-`5000`
- `name_lookup` (Boolean) Enable Name Lookup for OSPFv3 Neighbors.
- `passive_interface_default` (Boolean) Suppress routing updates on the interface.
- `router_id` (String) Router identifier for this VRF.

<a id="nestedatt--instances--vrfs--address_families"></a>
### Nested Schema for `instances.vrfs.address_families`

Optional:

- `administrative_distance` (String) Adminitrative distance. Value must be an integer range [1,255] or keyword: unspecified
- `default_information_originate_always` (Boolean) Always advertise default leak.
- `default_information_originate_route_map` (String) The name of the default route leak policy route map. This route map name is used to control distribution.
- `default_metric` (String) Default metric for redistributed routes. Value must be an integer range [0,16777214] or keyword: unspecified
- `default_route_nssa_pbit_clear` (Boolean) Override RFC 3101 behaviour and add default route on ABR even if P-bit is clear in received type-7 default route LSA.
- `max_ecmp_cost` (Number) Maximum Equal Cost Multi Path(ECMP).
  - Range: `1`-`64`
- `redistributions` (Attributes Map) List of OSPFv3 route redistributions.
  - Map key format: `<protocol>;<protocol_instance>;<asn>`
  - Key component `protocol`: The list of protocols to match. Choices: `unspecified`, `static`, `direct`, `bgp`, `isis`, `ospf`, `ospfv3`, `eigrp`, `host`, `rip`, `amt`, `lisp`, `hmm`, `am`, `srv6`, `dhcpv6`, `icmpv6`.
  - Key component `protocol_instance`: The inter protocol route leak policy instance.
  - Key component `asn`: The autonomous system number. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--instances--vrfs--address_families--redistributions))
- `spf_throttle_hold_interval` (Number) Minimum hold time interval between SPF calculations.
  - Range: `1`-`600000`
- `spf_throttle_initial_interval` (Number) Initial SPF schedule delay interval.
  - Range: `1`-`600000`
- `spf_throttle_max_interval` (Number) Maximum wait time between SPF calculations.
  - Range: `1`-`600000`
- `summary_addresses` (Attributes Map) List of OSPFv3 external route summarizations (summary-address).
  - Map key: `address` - Address. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--instances--vrfs--address_families--summary_addresses))

<a id="nestedatt--instances--vrfs--address_families--redistributions"></a>
### Nested Schema for `instances.vrfs.address_families.redistributions`

Optional:

- `route_map` (String) The name of the default route leak policy route map. This route map name is used to control distribution.
- `srv6_prefix_type` (String) SRv6 Prefix Type; Valid only when proto is srv6.
  - Choices: `unspecified`, `locator`


<a id="nestedatt--instances--vrfs--address_families--summary_addresses"></a>
### Nested Schema for `instances.vrfs.address_families.summary_addresses`

Optional:

- `control` (String) Summary address no advertise. Cannot be configured together with `tag`.
  - Choices: `unspecified`, `no-advertise`
- `tag` (Number) Route tag of external route.
  - Range: `0`-`4294967295`



<a id="nestedatt--instances--vrfs--areas"></a>
### Nested Schema for `instances.vrfs.areas`

Optional:

- `address_families` (Attributes Map) List of OSPFv3 area address families.
  - Map key: `address_family_type` - Unicast IP address family type.
  - Key choices: `ipv6-ucast` (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--instances--vrfs--areas--address_families))
- `nssa_translator_role` (String) Not-so-stubby area(NSSA) translator role.
  - Choices: `always`, `candidate`, `never`
- `redistribute` (Boolean) Send redistributed LSAs into NSSA area.
- `summary` (Boolean) Originate summary LSA into other areas.
- `suppress_forward_address` (Boolean) Supress forwarding address in translated LSA.
- `type` (String) Configure area type as NSSA or stub.
  - Choices: `regular`, `stub`, `nssa`

<a id="nestedatt--instances--vrfs--areas--address_families"></a>
### Nested Schema for `instances.vrfs.areas.address_families`

Optional:

- `cost` (String) Specify cost for default inter-area-prefix LSA. Value must be an integer range [0,16777215] or keyword: unspecified.
- `ranges` (Attributes Map) List of OSPFv3 inter-area route summarizations (area ranges).
  - Map key: `address` - Address. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--instances--vrfs--areas--address_families--ranges))

<a id="nestedatt--instances--vrfs--areas--address_families--ranges"></a>
### Nested Schema for `instances.vrfs.areas.address_families.ranges`

Optional:

- `control` (String) Summary address no advertise.
  - Choices: `unspecified`, `no-advertise`
- `cost` (String) Area range cost for route summarization. Value must be an integer range [0,16777216] or keyword: unspecified.






<a id="nestedatt--interfaces"></a>
### Nested Schema for `interfaces`

Optional:

- `admin_state` (String) The administrative state of the object or policy.
  - Choices: `enabled`, `disabled`
- `advertise_secondaries` (Boolean) Advertise secondary IPv6 addresses.
- `area` (String) Area associated with interface.
- `bfd_control` (String) Bidirectional Forwarding Detection (BFD) control.
  - Choices: `unspecified`, `enabled`, `disabled`
- `cost` (Number) Cost associated with interface.
  - Range: `0`-`65535`
- `dead_interval` (Number) Dead interval, interval during which at least one hello packet must be received from a neighbor before the router declares that neighbor as down.
  - Range: `0`-`65535`
- `hello_interval` (Number) Interval between hello packets that OSPFv3 sends on the interface.
  - Range: `1`-`65535`
- `instance_id` (Number) OSPFv3 instance identifier under interface.
  - Range: `0`-`255`
- `instance_name` (String) OSPFv3 instance name used with area command.
- `mtu_ignore` (Boolean) Disable OSPF MTU mismatch detection.
- `network_type` (String) Network Type, can be Point-to-point or Broadcast.
  - Choices: `none`, `p2p`, `bcast`
- `passive` (String) Suppress routing updates on the interface.
  - Choices: `none`, `enabled`, `disabled`
- `priority` (Number) Router priority, used in determining the designated router on this network.
  - Range: `0`-`255`
- `retransmit_interval` (Number) Retransmit interval, the time between LSA retransmissions.
  - Range: `1`-`65535`
- `transmit_delay` (Number) Transmit delay, estimated time needed to send an LSA update packet.
  - Range: `1`-`450`

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `identity` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to       = nxos_ospfv3.example
  identity = {}
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
### Identity Schema


#### Optional

- `device` (String) A device name from the provider configuration.

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
# Terraform's `import` block requires a non-empty `id` value, so this format cannot be used to
# import nxos_ospfv3 for the default device. Use the `terraform import` command
# below, or identity-based import shown above, instead.
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import nxos_ospfv3.example ""
```
